sections.h2: Your main selling options in Lauderdale Lakes
sections.html:
Three routes exist: an agent listing, a sale handled by you alone, or a direct purchase by an investor. Each trades speed against price and effort, so weigh the house's problems and your calendar first.

Broward County offices handle the records behind any sale here: the property appraiser, the tax collector and the clerk of the circuit court. The city covers local services.

  • Listings reward a clean, updated unit and patience through showings.
  • Going alone keeps the agent's share but hands you every contract and disclosure.
  • An investor purchase fits deferred repairs, occupied units, liens or a fixed deadline.

Lauderdale Lakes is a compact city of about four square miles in the middle of Broward County, centered on the crossroads of State Road 7 (US 441) and Oakland Park Boulevard. It incorporated on June 22, 1961, when roughly 300 people lived in a rural area of farms and grazing land, and the neighborhoods around the lakes that give the city its name filled in over the following two decades. Voters moved to a Mayor, City Commission and City Manager structure in March 1998. Police service comes from the Broward Sheriff's Office, with 107 of its personnel serving the city.

Commuters and investors both look at that central crossroads first, so use it in your listing.

  • Share the street and cross streets so buyers can place the house.
  • Note any lake or canal frontage on the survey.
  • Tell buyers whether the home sits near the State Road 7 corridor.

sections.h2: Selling with a tenant in the house
sections.html:
You can, but the lease keeps running after a sale contract is signed. A buyer either takes the unit with the tenant in it or waits for the landlord to end the tenancy through the notice steps in Chapter 83.

Notice lengths depend on the problem. Missed rent draws a 3-day demand (weekends and court holidays do not count), and a lease violation the tenant can fix draws 7 days to cure. Month-to-month tenancies end on 30 days' notice and year-to-year ones on 60. A lease cannot waive these rules, and delivery can be by mail, hand, e-mail or a copy left at the unit.

  • Ask each buyer in writing whether they accept the lease as is.
  • Pass the rent roll and deposit amount to the closing agent.
  • Keep a copy of each notice and proof of how it was delivered.

sections.h2: Broward property taxes and your closing
sections.html:
Value is fixed on January 1, bills follow in November, and your months of ownership are settled at closing. The Broward County Property Appraiser handles values and exemptions; call 954-357-6830 with questions.

Florida property tax calendar for a Broward home
WhenWhat happens
January 1Assessment date
March 1Deadline to file for exemptions
AugustNotice of Proposed Property Taxes mailed
25 days after the noticePetition window for a value challenge
NovemberTax bills mailed
April 1Unpaid taxes turn delinquent

Paying early earns a discount that shrinks from 4 percent in November to 1 percent in February. A buyer's first bill can run higher than yours because a sale returns the house to full assessed value (s. 193.155).

A vacant or worn house still sells, but the buyer pool changes, and an empty building draws extra attention from insurers, neighbors and code staff. Lenders balk at deferred repairs, while an investor prices the work and closes without an inspection fight.

A homestead exemption ends once the home is rented or stops being your permanent residence. If you moved out and the exemption still sits on your parcel, tell the property appraiser.

  • Walk the property and list defects before you accept any offer.
  • Check the Broward tax collector for unpaid balances.
  • Ask the title company about liens that could delay closing.

sections.h2: What if I am behind on the mortgage?
sections.html:
Florida foreclosures run through the courts, so you usually have time to sell before a judgment sale. After judgment, the clerk sets the auction between 20 and 35 days out unless the lender agrees to longer (s. 45.031).

Talk to your servicer and the closing agent about a payoff statement, and ask whether a short sale or an investor purchase fits your balance. Open every letter from the lender and the court, and write the response date on a calendar. Silence is the costliest choice, because deadlines keep running whether or not you answer. A housing counselor or a legal aid office can read the papers with you before you decide anything.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready to show
sections.html:
Start with what buyers notice from the curb: the roof line, the yard, the front door and any peeling paint. On an older house, buyers ask about the age of the roof, the electrical panel, the plumbing and the air handler. A one-page list of what was replaced and when answers those questions before they become negotiating points.

Clear out clutter and walk each room with a notepad. Note stains, soft floors, door-frame cracks and anything that smells of damp. Florida humidity punishes closed-up houses, so run the air conditioning and open the blinds before every showing.

Write each path as a net figure. For a listing, take the expected sale price and subtract the agent's commission, the repairs a buyer's inspector will demand, carrying costs for each month on the market, and closing costs. For an investor offer, subtract only what the contract assigns to you.

Then compare timing. A listing may take months and can fall through at financing or appraisal. An investor sale can close within a few weeks, but the price is lower. Ask any buyer to put these terms in writing, and read every line before signing.

  • Price, deposit and whether it is refundable.
  • Closing date and who picks the title company.
  • Who pays for repairs found in inspection.
  • What happens to any security deposit held for a tenant.

sections.h2: From signed contract to closing day
sections.html:
Once you accept an offer, the title company opens a search on the parcel. It looks for mortgages, judgments, unpaid taxes and anything recorded against your name. Clear what you can early, because a surprise lien is the most common reason a closing slips.

You will see a draft settlement statement before signing. Check the payoff, the prorated tax, recording charges and any fee the buyer expects you to cover. Bring photo ID and the names of every owner on the deed, since each one signs. If an owner lives out of state, arrange the signing ahead of time.

On closing day the deed is recorded with the Broward clerk, the lender is paid off and the remainder goes to you. Book final readings for utilities and hand over keys, garage openers and any warranty papers.

faqs.q: How big is the city and where is its center?
faqs.a: About four square miles, centered on State Road 7 (US 441) at Oakland Park Boulevard.

faqs.q: Can I sell while a tenant lives in the house?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease stays in force, so the buyer takes the house with the tenant or waits for a lawful notice process to end the tenancy (s. 83.56, s. 83.57). Put your chosen route in the sales contract so the title company and the tenant both know the plan.

faqs.q: Will the buyer inherit my capped assessment?
faqs.a: No. A sale is a change of ownership, so the property returns to just value the following January 1 (s. 193.155).

faqs.q: When do Broward tax bills go out?
faqs.a: In November. Unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1, so ask the Broward tax collector for an exact balance before closing.
Broward Sheriff's Office personnel, 107 of them, serve alongside city staff.
